key_insight: Cluster-weighted loss using K-Means or hierarchical clustering helps a deep surrogate model focus on hard-to-predict turbulence regions and improves Reynolds-stress regression.
engineering_relevance: This approach can improve data-driven subgrid turbulence closure models for solar convection simulations and other regression tasks with spatially varying error.
method: Train MLP and 3D CNN surrogates on high-resolution StellarBox quiet-Sun simulation data.
Compute cluster-specific prediction errors and use them to weight the training loss.
Compare K-Means and Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering against prior baselines.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that cluster-weighted training improved CNN performance by 34% lower MSE and a significantly higher R2 score across heights and depths.
watch_item: Cluster-based weighting may depend on the chosen clustering method and error distribution, so its benefits should be validated across datasets and simulation regimes.
paper_title: Cluster-Weighted Training of Deep Surrogate Models for Subgrid Turbulent Transport
